title: We Bless Thee for This Sacred Day
description: We Bless Thee for This Sacred Day in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Caroline Gilman wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 484, “The Day of Rest”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: We bless Thee for this sa-cred day, Thou who hast ev-ery bless-ing given, Which sends the dreams of earth a-way, And yields a glimpse of open-ing heaven.

lines: We bless Thee for this sacred day,
Thou who hast every blessing given,
Which sends the dreams of earth away,
And yields a glimpse of opening heaven.
Rich day of holy, thoughtful rest,
We would improve the calm repose;
And, in God's service truly blest,
Forget the world, its joys and woes.
Lord! may Thy truth, upon the heart,
Now fall and dwell as heavenly dew,
And flowers of grace in freshness start
Where once the weeds of error grew.
May prayer now lift her sacred wings,
Which bears her to the King of kings,
And rests her at his sheltering throne.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Caroline Gilman died in 1888.
credits: Words by Caroline Gilman (1794–1888), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
